snippet: Section 20 of Pakistan Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016: Whoever intentionally and publicly exhibits or transmits any information through any information system which he knows to be false, and intimidates or harms the reputation or privacy of a natural person, commits an offence punishable with imprisonment or fine.
source: Pakistan PECA 2016 (Section 20 - Offence against dignity of natural person)

snippet: Section 21 of Pakistan Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016: Cyber Stalking - Whoever with intent to coerce or intimidate or harass any person uses information system to follow or contact a person despite clear indication of disinterest, or monitors a person's internet use commits cyber stalking.

Section 24 of Pakistan Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016: Cyberbullying & Protection - Transmitting or displaying electronic communications that threaten, abuse, or incite violence or severe emotional distress against an individual or minor online is strictly prohibited under FIA Enforcement.

FIA Pakistan Cybercrime Wing Guidelines: Electronic threats, extortion, unauthorized dissemination of personal data, and severe online harassment must be reported immediately to the FIA Cybercrime Reporting Centre for digital forensic investigation and account restriction.
source: Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) Pakistan Cybercrime Wing Official Guidance

snippet: Platform Community Safety Guidelines: We do not tolerate cyberbullying, hate speech, or harassment. Content that targets individuals with malicious insults, threats of violence, unwanted sexual harassment, or derogatory attacks based on protected characteristics (race, gender, religion, origin) will result in warning, account mute, or permanent block.
source: Standard Online Platform Community Safety Policy

snippet: UNICEF Cyberbullying Prevention Guidance: Cyberbullying is bullying with the use of digital technologies. It can take place on social media, messaging platforms, gaming platforms and mobile phones. It is repeated behavior, aimed at scaring, angering or shaming those who are targeted.
source: UNICEF Official Cyberbullying Awareness & Educational Standard

snippet: Platform Anti-Harassment & Sarcastic Abuse Directive: Subtle, passive-aggressive, or sarcastic behavior designed to repeatedly target, exclude, or publicly humiliate a user constitutes actionable online harassment under our digital civility framework.
